series: Climate Fiscal Policy Brief No. 6.1 · October 2026
title: Measure Carbon Pricing by the Emissions It Cuts

slides.title: Measure Carbon Pricing by the Emissions It Cuts
slides.subtitle: The Total Effective Carbon Price: one carbon-tax equivalent for any policy mix
slides.message: Headline carbon prices add up explicit prices, so standards, subsidies and feebates score zero. The Total Effective Carbon Price is the uniform carbon tax that would cut emissions as much as the actual mix: $37 per tonne for a mix that explicit prices rate at $21.
slides.author: Stephen J. Stretton · writing in a personal capacity

slides.title: Explicit prices understate a stylized policy mix by almost half

slides.text: The mix: a $30/t carbon tax on power and industry, a $10/MWh renewable subsidy and a fuel standard cutting road-fuel carbon intensity by 2%. All numbers are stylized.

slides.title: The TECP is the uniform carbon tax that would cut emissions as much as the mix

points.lead: A $30 tax on every fuel is worth $30.
points.text: Any other instrument is worth the uniform tax that matches its effect, same baseline, same horizon.
Weil (2021) proposed it, and the IMF computes it with CPAT, one model run per policy.

points.lead: What is new: a closed form.
points.text: Weights from an energy balance, fuel prices and two elasticities per sector turn any package into one number.
switching to cleaner fuels, and using less energy. A short correction is within 2% of the full model.

slides.source: Weil (2021); Black et al. (2022); working paper 6.1, Propositions 1–3.

slides.title: The tax is worth more than its headline; the fuel standard far less than its price
slides.note: Instruments are scored alone, so they do not add to the mix. The subsidy costs $79 of budget per tonne avoided, yet adds $4: a cost-per-tonne measure would rank it the most ambitious instrument.
slides.source: Author's calculation, stylized economy; working paper 6.1, worked example; Carhart et al. (2022) for the comprehensive price.

slides.title: Common elasticity errors cancel; errors in demand elasticities alone do not
slides.note: The TECP is always above the $21 explicit price. Estimated emission cuts move far more: a third more under CPAT's demand elasticities.
slides.source: Author's calculation, 2,000 draws; working paper 6.1, calibration; paper 5.4.
